summary: On-prem private deploy: egress NIC UDP checksum offload corrupts DNS responses -> service discovery timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report repeated service discovery timeouts and long-tailed artifact fetch latency from on-prem Private deployment. Failures began after a recent scheduled maintenance window on the customer's edge appliances. Initial symptoms point to failed DNS lookups followed by many retries and fallback attempts, causing control-plane reconnects and occasional model pull timeouts.

Impact:
- Multiple inference nodes intermittently fail to resolve control-plane hostnames leading to 5-10s delays on startup and periodic reconnects.
- Artifact downloads fall back to presigned-URL retries and sometimes fail after exhausting retries, causing degraded throughput for FinNova's data-processing pipelines.
- Customer reported increased 429/503s in application telemetry during peak traffic windows.

Environment details:
- Private deployment (on-prem appliance) using VPX edge firewall + BGP to corporate WAN.
- Egress path goes through vendor-managed edge with NIC offload features enabled (hardware UDP checksum offload).
- Redwood agent version: 2.7.3-release, runtime 1.14.0.
- DNS: internal forwarder -> corporate recursive resolver -> public resolvers.

Observed timing: First reported 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC after vendor maintenance window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a serving node in the customer's on-prem cluster, run 'dig +tcp +time=2 example-controlplane.redwood.ai' repeatedly and measure response rates.
2) Simulate load by running parallel artifact prefetch requests for a medium-sized model (~6GB) and watch DNS/multi-retry behavior.
3) Toggle NIC UDP checksum offload on the node's egress interface (ethtool -K eth0 rx off tx off) to validate symptom change.
4) Capture tcpdump on egress interface while reproducing to compare UDP reply payloads vs in-kernel checksums.
5) Compare behavior across nodes behind different edge appliances (to rule out node-local misconfigurations).
logs_and_samples: Mar 09 02:18:11 agent[svc]: control-plane DNS lookup failed: timeout after 2s (retrying)
Mar 09 02:18:13 agent[svc]: artifact-prefetch attempt 3 -> presigned URL GET 504 (upstream timeout)
tcpdump sample (node-05 egress): UDP reply length=512 but UDP checksum 0x0000 (offloaded), payload contains truncated DNS answer at byte 476
strace of resolver: recvfrom returned 512 bytes, resolver marks as SERVFAIL due to bad RDATA (length mismatch)
Vendor edge appliance config excerpt provided by customer (anonymized) shows hardware-accelerated UDP checksum handling enabled on egress interface.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ellen Rivera (Support): Initial triage completed. Customer seeing DNS failures correlating with vendor maintenance. Asking for packet captures and node-level ethtool output.

2026-03-10 13:45 - FinNova Network Ops (customer): Provided pcap + edge config. We toggled NIC offload on one host and timeouts stopped for that host. Other hosts still affected behind the vendor appliance.

2026-03-11 02:02 - Maya Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally in lab with a virtualized 'offloading' shim that zeroed checksums — DNS replies appeared malformed to userspace resolvers while correct on wire. Hypothesis: double offload/MTU interaction truncates DNS UDP payloads leading to resolver decoding errors.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Maya Chen (SRE): Requested vendor to validate firmware version; vendor responded they enabled a new optimization during maintenance which coalesces UDP checksums for large payloads (EDNS0/DNSSEC) and has a known issue with replies >480 bytes on certain NIC+firmware combos.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Customer: Confirmed enabling TCP fallback in resolver mitigates but customer FW blocks outbound TCP53 at perimeter (corporate policy). They will allow temporary exception for TCP53 for validation window.
2026-03-14 11:05 - Maya Chen (SRE): Coordinating with Networking and Vendor. Preparing mitigation steps and a postmortem draft.
investigation_notes: Packet analysis shows on-wire DNS UDP payloads that appear well-formed but include zeroed or mismatched checksum fields when the vendor offload + firmware optimization are active.

Userspace resolver receives buffer with truncated RDATA (length mismatch) and treats as SERVFAIL; application retries escalate to TCP fallback which is blocked at customer's perimeter, causing long tail and eventual artifact download failures.
Disabling NIC UDP checksum offload on host removes symptom immediately (local mitigation).
Reproduction in lab using a virtual NIC with checksum 'zeroing' reproduces resolver decode errors; confirms issue is in the offload/firmware layer rather than Redwood agent code.
Related configuration: EDNS0 with large UDP DNS responses for our control-plane SRV/TXT records and DNSSEC-signed resolver zones increase likelihood of >512B UDP responses.
Edge vendor acknowledged regression in firmware v3.12.8 introduced in maintenance; they have a patch pending but no ETA on customer timelines.

Workarounds considered: 1) Disable UDP checksum offload on all agent hosts (node-level) 2) Configure corporate perimeter to allow TCP53 to permit resolver fallback 3) Reduce EDNS0 advertised size (not ideal) 4) Use local DNS cache with TCP support (requires infra changes).
Customer reports production constraints: rolling restart of all nodes to flip offload is disruptive; customer prefers perimeter TCP53 exception short-term.
Added monitoring dashboard to track DNS SERVFAIL rate and artifact-prefetch retry counts; alert thresholds set to P1 paging.
Linked internal INT- tickets created for SRE playbook and vendor comms (see linked_issues).
resolution: Mitigation applied: Customer allowed temporary outbound TCP53 from agent subnets to corporate resolver (permitted 2026-03-13 22:00 - 2026-03-20), which immediately reduced timeouts and artifact failures.

Recommended short-term fix: Disable UDP checksum offload on egress-facing agent hosts where operationally feasible (ethtool -K eth0 rx off tx off). Customer will schedule a staggered maintenance window to apply this across nodes next week.
Long-term: Vendor to roll firmware patch to correct UDP coalescing behavior for large DNS responses. SRE to validate once patch available.
